commentary:
1. SCORE & MOMENTUM
The New Orleans Pelicans head into the locker room with a commanding 56-45 lead after outscoring Dallas in both opening quarters. New Orleans has dictated the pace, capitalizing on a significant efficiency gap by shooting 46.8% from the field compared to Dallas’s stagnant 36.4%.

2. KEY PLAYER ANALYSIS
Jeremiah Fears has been the catalyst for the Pelicans, contributing 12 points and orchestrating the offense with 5 assists. Conversely, John Poulakidas has struggled to find his rhythm, tallying only 9 points while the Dallas starters have failed to record a single assist.

3. X-FACTORS / FOUL TROUBLE
Ball security is the primary culprit for Dallas, as they have committed 13 turnovers to New Orleans’s 6, leading to a lopsided 1.00 to 2.67 AST/TO ratio. While Dallas has been aggressive on the glass with a +5 rebound differential and 25 bench points, their foul trouble—with five more fouls than the Pelicans—is preventing them from sustaining any defensive momentum.

4. SECOND-HALF OUTLOOK
The Pelicans are in total control and will secure a 6-point victory by maintaining their superior 0.543 eFG%. Dallas must drastically improve their 24% shooting from deep and protect the basketball to avoid this inevitable outcome. Expect New Orleans to continue exploiting their clinical passing to close out the game as predicted.
